newsitem.title: USA: US natgas stocks seen up 65-70 bcf in weekly AGAs.
newsitem.headline: US natgas stocks seen up 65-70 bcf in weekly AGAs.

text.p: U.S. natural gas storage levels were expected to rise by 65 to 70 billion cubic feet (bcf) when weekly American Gas Association (AGA) data are released later today, industry sources said Wednesday.
The Reuter poll of industry players showed expectations for an overall build ranged from 43 bcf to 90 bcf for the week ended October 11. The four-week average is 88 bcf.
"We had (Tropical Storm) Josephine and the weather last week was as cold as the week before, so I don't expect the number to be anywhere near last week's," a Houston-based trader said.

Last week, AGA showed overall storage rose by an unexpected 94 bcf, well-above expectations, but was still 229 bcf, or eight percent, below the same year-ago period. Eastern stocks rose to 89 percent of capacity and should match or exceed 1995 levels, traders said.
But producing region inventories at 70 percent full continued to lag last year by about 17 percent.

Last year at this time, total inventories gained 70 bcf, meaning a build today in the expected range would leave the gap to 1995 roughly unchanged. For the same week in 1995, eastern storage rose by 45 bcf, while producing stocks were up 18 bcf.
Most agreed Tropical Storm Josephine, which last week forced the shut in of more than 10 bcf of U.S. Gulf gas production, likely trimmed net injections for the week.
-- J Silha, New York Power Desk 212-859-1624
